Ocean silicate: partially observed oxygen inputs

  • 1. Computation settings
  • 2. Data and observation design
  • 3. Model fitting and numerical assessment
  • 4. Response prediction
  • 5. Response functions
  • 6. Training-input imputation
  • 7. Reproducibility and references

This semi-real application evaluates silicate prediction with partially observed oxygen inputs. Measured records are retained as references; ordinal records and nested measurement masks are constructed on a fixed, class-balanced cohort.

1. Computation settings

  • Action: plan lists tasks; run fits or resumes; report reads saved fits.
  • Dataset: ocean200, ocean500 or ocean1000; prepare the 1000-profile folds once using data/ocean_silicate/prepare_folds.R.
  • Selection: folds, cells and modules select tasks without changing seeds or numerical settings.
  • Distributed runs: use separate result roots and merge compatible tasks through import_dirs.

Runnable examples are in README_ocean.md.

Profile: quick; action: run; folds: 1; training calibration: 0%, 20%, 50%.

Selected work: 9 base tasks and 0 conditional continuation candidates.

Initial EIV numerical settings: 1 chains, 80 iterations per chain, 30 burn-in iterations. Native comparator controls are read from saved fitting records and listed with the results.

2. Data and observation design

Notation

Symbol Application variable
\(y\) Silicate response
\(u\) Continuous oxygen input
\(c\) Ordinal oxygen record: \([0,50),[50,100),[100,150),[150,180)\)
\(x\) Salinity and natural-log pressure

Concentrations are in micromol/kg. In test tables, \((x,c)\) denotes inputs without observed \(u\); \((x,u)\) denotes inputs with observed \(u\).

Data-use protocols

The suffixes describe how training records and test inputs are used. Native comparators retain \(c\) as a categorical input when \(u\) is observed.

  • OI (ordinal-input protocol): Use all training profiles; predict from (x,c) for every test profile.
  • CC (complete-case protocol): Fit only training profiles with observed u; evaluate only test profiles with observed u.
  • MI (mixed-input protocol): Use all training profiles; use (x,u) where test u is observed and (x,c) otherwise.

Test-input percentages are computed from the observation masks; sample counts are reported separately in the design and results tables.

Cohort construction

  • Source: GLODAPv2.2023 Pacific merged and adjusted product; 10–50 degrees N, 140–240 degrees E.
  • Quality filters: finite temperature/salinity, positive oxygen, and oxygen/silicate/nitrate flags equal to 2. Nitrate is not a predictor.
  • Analysis domain: pressure 300–1500 dbar and \(0<u<180\).
  • Sampling unit: one bottle per cruise–station profile. Selection balances the four \(c\) levels, within-level oxygen quartiles and log-pressure halves.

The class boundaries specify an imposed recording rule, not oceanographic regimes. The cohort followed exploratory screening; frozen folds subsequently balanced input strata and salinity without using responses.

The selected cohort contains 200 profiles from 108 cruises, with actual ranges 10.002–48.991 degrees N, 140.21–179.08 degrees E and 300.8–1486.5 dbar.

Training and test information

  • Per fold: 160 training and 40 test profiles, with 40/10 per \(c\) level.
  • Training: \((x,c,y)\) observed for all 160 profiles. O0/O20/O50 additionally reveal \(u\) for 0/32/80 profiles; nested subsets retain cut-side anchors.
  • Testing: either \((x,c)\) for all profiles, or \((x,u)\) for 8/20 profiles and \((x,c)\) for the remainder. Test masks are nested, class-balanced up to integer rounding, and identical across methods.
  • Separation: test \(y\) is excluded from fitting/tuning. Transformations use training data; \(u\) scaling uses training calibration measurements. Hidden reference \(u\) is used only for design, evaluation and offline plots.
Observed information per fold
Training exact U Training profiles Exact training U Test N: (x,c) Partial-u test: (x,u) N Partial-u test: (x,c) N
0% 160 0 40 0 40
20% 160 32 40 8 32
50% 160 80 40 20 20

All training y observed; all test y withheld. The partial-u condition is evaluated at O20/O50 only. Test masks use seed 202609260 + fold.

EIV-GP targets and comparator scope

The EIV-GP hierarchy defines the targets below; comparators share only the applicable response targets.

\[m_{f,\psi}(x,c)=\int f(x,u)Q_\psi(du\mid x,c).\]

Target Evaluation and comparator scope
Held-out \(y\) prediction All methods are scored on matched profiles and available inputs. EIV-GP uses \(p(y^*\mid x^*,c^*,D)\) or \(p(y^*\mid x^*,u^*,D)\); baselines use native predictors.
Observable mean \(m(x,c)\) EIV-GP integrates its conditional \(u\) law; original \((x,c)\) baselines estimate the recorded-input mean directly. True \(m\) is unavailable.
Calibrated surface \(f(x,u)\) Displayed for EIV-GP. CC comparators define their own response functions of \((x,u,c)\); these are not the same EIV hierarchy. True \(f\) is unavailable.
Training-input posterior \(p(u_i\mid D)\) EIV-GP only; uses training \(y_i\) and is evaluated against masked reference \(u_i\). Baselines provide no individual physical-input posterior.

Conclusions concern this selected cohort and imposed observation design. Profiles are disjoint across training/test sets, but cruises can overlap; new-cruise or regional transfer, natural missingness and causal effects are not established.

3. Model fitting and numerical assessment

The following chunk executes the selected action and saves predictions/imputations.

if (settings$action == "plan") {
  analysis <- ocean_analysis(repository_dir, data_dir, output_dir, settings)
} else {
  analysis <- ocean_logged(
    file.path(output_dir, "jobs", settings$run_id, "execution.log"),
    ocean_analysis(
      repository_dir, data_dir, output_dir, settings,
      import_dirs = import_dirs, cc_output_dir=cc_output_dir,
      diagnostics_dir=diagnostics_dir,representative_fold=params$representative_fold,
      diagnostics_workers=params$diagnostics_workers
    )
  )
}
  • EIV-GP: a joint response/input model with deterministic ordinal thresholds. The working input population is standard Gaussian and independent of \(x\).
  • Native comparators: UC-GP, LVGP and EzGP use all training \((x,c,y)\) records for OI, or only complete \((x,u,c,y)\) records for CC. Complete-case continuous inputs are standardized using that training subset.
  • Test scope: complete-case methods and EIV-GP are compared on the same observed-\(u\) test subset. The mixed-input EIV rule additionally predicts the entire test set. No missing test \(u\) is filled for the complete-case methods.
  • Result roots: output_dir supplies EIV/recorded-input fits; cc_output_dir supplies independently verified CC tasks.
Fold 0% exact U 20% exact U 50% exact U
1 Initial saved Initial saved Initial saved
Supplementary: computation and posterior approximation
  • Package calls: the run_eiv() routine created by ocean_initial_functions() in the Ocean section of eivGP/R/helpers.R calls fit_eivgp(), predict_eivgp() and impute_eivgp(); selected continuations call continue_eivgp().
  • Native baselines: the pinned run_published_mixedgp_competitors() adapter calls kergp, LVGP and EzGP fitting/prediction routines. CC package_status.csv retains optimizer status and warnings. A finite prediction can be returned with a flagged optimizer code; task completion alone does not establish optimizer convergence.
  • Continuation rule: one extra 20,000 iterations if initial maximum finite Rhat exceeds 1.01, minimum finite bulk ESS is below 400, or finite values are unavailable; u_block_size=8.
  • Review: finite diagnostics, tail ESS and undefined values are reported separately. Passing the screen does not establish model adequacy, identification or precision of every functional.

4. Response prediction

For EIV-GP, prediction means average \(m(x,c)\) for \((x,c)\) inputs and \(f(x,u)\) for \((x,u)\) inputs. The tables score held-out \(y\), not true \(m/f\) recovery.

  • RMSE: point prediction error; CRPS: predictive-distribution loss (lower is better).
  • Coverage/width: 95% response intervals. EIV-GP includes response noise, posterior uncertainty and unresolved \(u\); native baselines include fitted noise/nugget without integrating missing physical \(u\).
  • Normalization: \(s_Y\) is the frozen cohort response SD, used only to scale reported scores/widths. Method suffixes follow the data-use protocols defined in Section 2. For EIV-GP, OI uses \(m(x,c)\); MI routes between \(m(x,c)\) and \(f(x,u)\) according to observed test information.

Complete-case comparison

Each CC comparator is fitted only to training profiles with observed \(u\), using continuous \((x,u)\), categorical \(c\) and response \(y\). Training profiles without measured \(u\) are omitted. EIV-GP retains all training profiles.

Within each calibration condition, all methods are evaluated on the same test profiles with observed \(u\). EIV-GP(MI) uses its \(f(x,u)\) route on this subset. These subset scores have a different evaluation population from the preceding all-profile table.

5. Response functions

These fitted associations are shown on the representative fold, with nearby measured profiles for context. Shading is a pointwise 95% credible interval for the mean, excluding response noise; it is not a response prediction interval.

Observable mean m(x,c)

  • Slice: salinity 34.20; vary pressure within each \(c\) level.
  • Comparison: EIV O0/O20/O50 and original \((x,c)\) baselines; \(m\) integrates the fitted conditional \(u\) distribution.

Calibrated response function f(x,u)

  • Slice: salinity 34.25, pressure 650 dbar; vary \(u\) over the central range of nearby reference profiles.
  • Interpretation: O20/O50 provide calibrated coordinates; nearby observations do not guarantee dense joint support. This differs from the \(x\) slice used for \(m\).

Point markers: filled = training; hollow = test. Blue rings identify training calibration shared by O20/O50; orange rings identify additional O50 calibration. Masked \(u\) is positioned using offline references only. Nearby profiles have varying \(x\) and noisy responses, so their distance from a mean band is not a coverage diagnostic. These plots do not establish true-surface recovery.

Supplementary: response functions across folds

6. Training-input imputation

The posterior \(p(u_i\mid D)\) uses training \(y_i\). Evaluation compares O20/O50 on the same 80 hidden training profiles per fold; it does not assess prospective \(u\) prediction without \(y\). O0 is shown on its unanchored working coordinate.

Hollow points are observed calibration inputs; solid points and intervals summarize hidden-input posteriors. Overall bias can conceal opposing class biases, and narrower intervals alone do not establish better calibration.

Marginal distribution of hidden training inputs

  • Solid curve: pool the posterior draws of the same 80 hidden profiles, with equal weight per profile.
  • Gray histogram: the actual measured \(u\) values of those 80 profiles, withheld from fitting; bar area represents empirical frequency. Rug marks individual measurements.
  • O0: posterior draws remain in model units. There is no training calibration to identify a physical oxygen scale, so raw measured \(u\) cannot be overlaid. O20/O50 use physical units and identical reference histograms.

Compare location, spread and tails with the measured distribution. This marginal check includes between-profile variation; individual interval calibration remains assessed by the preceding imputation plot and coverage summaries.

Class-specific imputation calibration

The model learns cutpoints; its extreme categories are unbounded. Individual-U intervals can therefore exceed the constructed \(c\) intervals or cohort bounds. Detailed counts are provided below without clipping intervals.

Supplementary: class-specific imputed-input distributions
  • Solid curve: equally weighted mixture of the individual \(u_i\) posteriors within each \(c\).
  • Gray histogram / rug: empirical distribution / individual measured values for the same 20 hidden profiles per class. These values are withheld from fitting.
  • Columns: O0/O20/O50 on the same 80 common-hidden profiles. O0 remains in model units; O20/O50 share histogram bins, physical axes and posterior smoothing within each class.
  • Reading: compare location, spread and tails with references. Marginal spread includes differences between individuals; it cannot establish individual posterior contraction or coverage. Increasing calibration need not narrow every distribution.
Supplementary: individual-input interval support

An interval is counted when either endpoint lies outside the constructed \(c\) interval. This checks support compatibility, not reference-value coverage or posterior probability outside the interval. Learned model cutpoints differ from the construction boundaries; the extreme model categories have unbounded endpoints and do not enforce \(0<u<180\).

Supplementary: training-input imputation across folds

7. Reproducibility and references

  • Execution: task seeds are independent of assignment/order; receipts validate reuse and merging. Logs are under jobs/<run_id>/.
  • Prediction evidence: prediction_report/cc_revision/ contains current recorded-input/CC/EIV scores and EIV-only matched-input evidence. Each CC task records the precise training/test IDs, transforms, controls, seed and native status.
  • Input distributions: diagnostics/u_distributions/ records common-hidden profile references and plotted density curves; posterior states are thinned deterministically for visualization only.
  • Posterior review: diagnostics/refinement/ contains input-support checks, diagnostic exceptions and selected full-chain MCSE.
  • Pending experiments: PI-GP, additional calibration masks and formal UC-GP optimization are not included in these results.

The HTML embeds its figures. Environment requirements and provenance are in README_ocean.md.

Data: GLODAPv2.2023, DOI 10.25921/zyrq-ht66. Product reference: Lauvset et al. (2024), Earth System Science Data 16, 2047–2072, DOI 10.5194/essd-16-2047-2024.
